model_note: Every forecast version in forecasts.csv and scores.csv carries the model that produced it in the model column: gbm:<file> for a stored model, with the suffix :fallback when the default model's inputs were missing and the fallback model was used, and gbm for a model fitted live.

default.scored_against: the auction result; the EEX traded price is the only benchmark (Versus the market)

previous.scored_against: the auction result; the EEX traded price is the only benchmark (Versus the market)

live_record.rule: Each delivery day counts once, scored against the auction result on the last version issued before the market window opened (11:15 Paris on the day before); a day whose versions were all issued later is listed as late only and not scored. The record is the current default model from its first pre-market day; the earlier days of the previous set are a separate row. It states the model's own error only: the EEX traded price, in the Versus the market panel, is the one benchmark of the level forecast.

recent_check.note: a check on the last days before the fit, scored by a model fitted without them; the stored file was then fitted on all rows including these days, so this is not an out-of-sample result for the stored file and not the frozen holdout of docs/experiments.md

frozen_holdout.method: monthly walk-forward, backtest settings, not this file

recent_check.note: a check on the last days before the fit, scored by a model fitted without them; the stored file was then fitted on all rows including these days, so this is not an out-of-sample result for the stored file and not the frozen holdout of docs/experiments.md

frozen_holdout.method: monthly walk-forward, backtest settings, not this file

market.source: EEX French Day-Ahead Base and Peak futures traded before the auction, collected locally; traded prices are not republished.
market.benchmark: the only benchmark of the level forecast: the window VWAP of the traded future, scored at the auction result
market.counts: windows (one per delivery day and product, base or peak) of settled delivery days whose published pre-market version of the default set (the version shown on the public site, read from published/forecasts.csv on main) was issued before the market window (11:15 Paris on the trade date), scored against the auction result; days whose published versions were all issued later, days with only a local version on the collecting machine, and days without a traded price are not counted; the backfilled walk-forward record in the README (42 windows) is a separate, out-of-sample reissue, not part of this count
market.note: Versus the market: collecting data, 15 of 20 days.
market.carried_note: this machine holds no traded prices; the aggregates are the last ones computed on the laptop

calibration.method: isotonic regression (increasing, clipped to [0, 1]) of the outcome on the raw probability, fitted on out-of-sample pairs only: walk-forward backtest predictions and settled live pre-market versions; refitted monthly with the models; applied to the raw probability at issue time

definitions.negative: probability that the hour's price is below zero, from a classifier on the same inputs as the point forecast; accepted on the selection window and confirmed on the holdout (docs/experiments.md)

attributions: Day-ahead prices, load forecast and wind and solar forecasts: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform, https://transparency.entsoe.eu, reused with the source cited as required by its terms.
French load history used in the thermosensitivity work: RTE eCO2mix via ODRE, https://opendata.reseaux-energies.fr, Licence Ouverte v2.0 (Etalab).
Weather forecasts: Open-Meteo.com, https://open-meteo.com, CC BY 4.0.
note: Forecasts use only information available at 12:00 Paris time on the day before delivery. The level forecast has one benchmark: the EEX French day-ahead future traded before the auction, scored at the auction result, as aggregates under "market" once enough windows are recorded (hit rate, mean P&L per MWh, model and market error, window count). Forecast error (MAE) is the model's own error against the auction result, with no other comparison. Traded prices are not republished. Historical errors are shown as context, not as a probability forecast.
